title: Exclusive: American detained in Cuba for nearly a decade quietly released | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

An American held for nearly a decade in Cuba was quietly released earlier this year, two sources familiar with the matter and a State Department spokesperson told CNN.

Alina López Miyares’s release, which has not been previously reported, came amid soaring tensions between Washington and Havana, as the Trump administration has ratcheted up its pressure campaign to try to force changes to the government there.

According to the sources, a US government team quietly flew to Havana to bring López back to the United States. According to one of the sources and the State Department spokesperson, the US government did not pay or exchange anything with Cuba to secure the release 68-year-old Cuban American teacher, who was detained in 2017 and accused of espionage.

“We welcomed Alina López return to the United States in September. There was no exchange for her release. Out of respect for her privacy, we have nothing further at this time,” the spokesperson told CNN.

López’s legal team, which includes her longtime Washington, DC,  attorney Jason Poblete and South Florida litigator Dylan Barket, had no comment and asked for privacy for their client.

CNN has reached out to the Cuban Embassy in Washington, DC, and the Cuban foreign ministry for comment.

López was born in Cuba but left as a child. She became a US citizen and worked as a special education teacher. According to advocates, she was lured to Cuba in 2017 by her estranged husband, who they say was a Cuban spy, and detained. She was charged with espionage and sentenced by a military court to 13 years in prison.

In 2022, the UN Human Rights Council Working Group on Arbitrary Detention ruled that López was arbitrarily detained and called for her immediate release.

A State Department official told CNN in March that the Trump administration had raised her case with Cuban officials and advocated for her to be freed on humanitarian grounds. It is unclear at what level it was raised with the Cubans.

Michael Peralta, López’s son, said in March that his mother faced significant health challenges that possibly required surgery. Her detention was causing the family “a lot of emotional and mental strain. López missed the burials of her parents, he told CNN at the time.

“My grandmother, while she was still alive, for several years was in her late 80s and early 90s, was visiting my mother once a month by herself, taking her food and medicine. I’m pretty sure that there was more rapid deterioration for her due to the stress and how emotionally distraught she was. Same for my grandfather. Seems like his like he aged a lot faster than one would have expected,” Peralta said.

“She’s desperate to come home,” he said. “She just keeps praying every day that she’ll be back home and close to us here in Florida, back in the United States, sometime soon.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio was supportive of the effort to free López, the sources said. As top US diplomat, Rubio has led the administration’s campaign to try to pressure the Castro government in Havana to cede power. US sanctions on the island and blockade on oil shipments have further paralyzed the Cuban economy and exacerbated its already critical power situation, leading to months of rolling blackouts.

CNN’s Boris Sanchez and Patrick Oppmann contributed to this report.
